content: The Sparkling Enope Squid, scientifically known as Watasenia scintillans and commonly referred to as the Firefly Squid, belongs to the class Cephalopoda, subclass Coleoidea, and order Teuthida. It is the only species within the genus Watasenia. This squid inhabits the Western Pacific Ocean at depths ranging from 600 to 1200 feet. It exhibits bioluminescent properties, with specialized light-producing organs called photophores located on each of its tentacles. By emitting flashes of light from these photophores, the squid is able to attract small fish, which it preys upon. Remarkably, the Sparkling Enope Squid is the only known cephalopod species to possess evidence of color vision. While most cephalopods have a single visual pigment, this species has three visual pigments and a double-layered retina. These adaptations are thought to have evolved to help the squid differentiate between ambient light and bioluminescent signals in its environment. At full maturity, the Sparkling Enope Squid measures approximately 3 inches in length. Its lifespan is relatively short, lasting only about one year. During mating, the squid can illuminate its entire body to attract a mate. The mating season occurs between March and June.
